claims.text: A short post-solidification anneal can improve the tensile ductility and uniform elongation of HfZrTiTa0.53 while preserving strength and impact-triggered energy release.
The initial HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is in an as-solidified condition.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a baseline yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a baseline compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a baseline terminal strain of approximately 13.5%.
An intermediate-temperature anneal at 400–500 °C for 15–30 minutes is a suitable intervention window.
The proposed anneal produces localized residual-stress relief.
The proposed anneal makes the microstructure more homogeneous.
The proposed anneal improves grain-boundary cohesion.
Thermal activation during annealing enables dislocation rearrangement and recovery of as-solidified defects.
Defect recovery and stress relief reduce microcrack-nucleation sites.
Reducing microcrack-nucleation sites enhances uniform plastic deformation under tensile loading.
The short anneal will not significantly alter the alloy's intrinsic phase stability.
The alloy's intrinsic phase stability enables its high compressive strength.
The alloy's intrinsic phase stability enables impact-triggered energy release.
Annealing will raise uniform tensile elongation to greater than 15%.
Annealing will maintain yield strength within approximately 10% of 786 MPa.
Annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 will match the impact energy-release performance of the as-solidified alloy.
The expected benefit applies at room temperature under quasi-static tensile loading near 10^-3 s^-1 and may not extend to substantially different temperatures or strain rates.
Excessive annealing-induced grain coarsening could degrade mechanical strength.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is identified as terminal strain in the initial-state and baseline fields but is then treated as the baseline for uniform elongation in the predicted outcome. Terminal strain and uniform tensile elongation are not interchangeable metrics.
